data.raw_response:
=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): alternate (leaves are attached at successive nodes along the stem, alternating sides)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): clustered (leaves are densely packed at the terminal ends of the stems)
B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): compound (leaflets are arranged along a central axis, rachis)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): odd-pinnate (a single terminal leaflet is present at the apex of the leaf)
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): 13 (estimated from the largest fully visible leaf structure)
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): alternate (leaflets are arranged alternately along the rachis)
C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.): entire (the leaflet margins appear smooth and continuous, despite some physical damage)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): lanceolate (leaflets are linear to lance-shaped, widest below the middle and tapering towards the tip)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acuminate (leaflets taper to a distinct, elongated point at the tip)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): cuneate (leaflets taper gradually to a wedge-shaped base where they attach to the rachis)
    11. Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (a single midrib runs down the center of each leaflet with veins branching off)
    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): clearly visible, pinnate, spaced relatively closely and regularly along the midrib
    13. Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): glabrous, slightly shiny (the leaflets appear smooth and lack hairiness, with a slight sheen)
    14. Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs or trichomes on the leaf surface)
    15. Petiole length (short / long): short (the petiole connecting the leaf to the stem is very short and not prominently elongated)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (the petiole appears cylindrical and round in cross-section)
D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): woody (the stems appear rigid, brown, and somewhat lignified)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (the stem surface appears smooth and hairless)
    19. Stem color: brown (the visible stems are a light to medium brown color)
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (the stem surface appears relatively even without prominent ridges or lenticels)
E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no stipules are clearly visible at the leaf bases)
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed (no latex is visible)
    23. Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): not observed (no pulvinus is clearly visible at the petiole-rachis or petiole-stem junctions)
    24. Tendrils (present / absent): absent (no tendrils are visible on the seedling)
F. Notes: The seedling exhibits compound leaves with alternate leaflets. Some leaflets show minor damage, including holes and brown spots. The background consists of leaf litter.
